item.title: You don't get to close the office door
item.description:
A reflection on remote work, boundaries, and the slow art of keeping your evenings yours

I’ve been working remotely, on and off, for the better part of ten years. And in that time, the shape of the problem has changed completely — but the problem itself has stayed the same: how do you stop work from eating the rest of your life when there’s no door to walk out of?

item.title: The paradox of modern work: Why finishing never feels finished
item.description:
I remember reading a blog post years ago, something along the lines of “Busyness is a modern symptom of life.” I was 18 or 19 years old at that time, and I didn’t really get it. Back then, work had borders. You showed up, did the thing, and left. When the day ended, your brain followed.

Busyness felt like a choice other people were making.
